# Proposal: Practitioner Academy for Tamarack Instruments

**Prepared for:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel
**Program:** Practitioner Academy, AI Governance Academy
**Basis:** Discovery call of 6 October 2026

## Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments from its headquarters in the Netherlands, with operations in Germany and the United States. It is building AI capability in three stages:

* **Deployed:** a customer service chatbot on the support portal.
* **Piloting:** AI visual inspection on the German production line.
* **Planned:** AI sales forecasting next year.

Two pressures meet in 2027. First, you have set a clear objective: governance must be in place before visual inspection enters production in Q2 2027. Second, the June 2026 internal audit finding recorded that Tamarack has no inventory of AI systems.

The EU AI Act and GDPR frame the regulatory exposure. ISO/IEC 42001 work is expected to begin next year, though the start date is not yet fixed.

Tamarack already has two strong foundations: an ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS and an ISO 9001 quality management system. The task is not to build governance from nothing. It is to extend disciplines Tamarack already runs so they cover AI systems.

## Why Hands-On Practitioner Capability Fits Now

Tamarack's maturity is Piloting. At this stage, governance decisions made now are cheap to shape and expensive to retrofit later. Your objective points to a specific deadline, a specific system and a specific site. That favors working sessions that produce usable artifacts over awareness training.

The Practitioner Academy places your General Counsel, CISO, Head of Quality, Head of Data, German plant manager and two internal auditors in the same working sessions. Each participant works directly in the GRC Workbook and Slow AI Kitchen repositories, so the team leaves knowing where every artifact lives and how to continue without outside help.

The program is anchored in three principles: **Slow AI**, **Informed Intent** and **Final Liability rests with the Human**.

## Running Worked Examples

**Selection 1: AI visual inspection (German production line).** This is the primary example. It is the system named in your objective and it carries the Q2 2027 deadline. It also engages the Head of Quality and the plant manager directly and sits inside the ISO 9001 change discipline.

**Selection 2: Customer service chatbot.** This is the secondary example. It is the only system already in production and it handles customer interactions. That brings in GDPR, the EU data residency constraint and the CISO's ISMS controls. It also gives the team a contrast between governing a live system and governing a pilot.

**Inventory and classification only: AI sales forecasting.** This system is planned rather than built. It enters the inventory and classification exercise so it is captured before procurement or development begins. It is not carried through the full two days.

## Two-Day Curriculum

The program runs as two days, live virtual, with four 90-minute working sessions each day. Day 1 uses the GRC Workbook. Day 2 uses the Slow AI Kitchen plus assurance work.

| Session | Focus | Tamarack Worked Example | Repository |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Governance structures | Opens with *The Turtle and the Phoenix* to seat the doctrine. Then map decision rights for AI across Legal, Security, Quality, Data and the German plant. | GRC Workbook |
| 2 | AI system inventories and classification | Start the Tamarack AI inventory with all three systems. Draft EU AI Act classification reasoning for each, for counsel review. | GRC Workbook |
| 3 | Risk and impact assessments | Draft risk register entries for visual inspection and the chatbot, aligned to the existing ISMS and QMS risk methods. | GRC Workbook |
| 4 | Policies and operating procedures | Draft an AI use procedure that links to existing ISO 9001 change control and ISO/IEC 27001 controls. | GRC Workbook |
| 5 | Governed prompting | Build governed prompts for chatbot responses and escalation rules. | Slow AI Kitchen |
| 6 | Practical AI workflow design | Design governed workflows for inspection defect review and chatbot escalation. | Slow AI Kitchen |
| 7 | Human oversight and accountability | Define who reviews, overrides and signs off inspection outcomes, with named accountable roles. | Slow AI Kitchen |
| 8 | Evidence collection and audit readiness | With the two internal auditors, define the evidence each artifact must produce. Test it against the June 2026 inventory finding. | Slow AI Kitchen plus GRC Workbook |

The fable's handle map connects the story to the workbook modules, so the principles carry from Day 1 into the instruments used on Day 2.

## Respecting Tamarack's Constraints

**Customer data.** Exercises use sanitized analogs only. Chatbot work uses synthetic support-portal conversations instead of real customer transcripts. No customer data is requested, shared or moved outside the EU.

**Production staff and the works council.** Visual inspection work uses synthetic defect images and synthetic inspection logs. Nothing produced in the program is deployed or applied to production staff. The inspection workflow designed in Session 6 will include German works council consultation as an explicit gate before any production use.

Tamarack should confirm internally whether the plant manager's participation itself requires any works council notice. That requirement is currently Unknown to us.

## Deliverables

By the close of Day 2, Tamarack will hold the following working drafts. Each will have a named internal owner responsible for finishing it.

1. **A started AI system inventory** covering the chatbot, visual inspection and sales forecasting, with draft classification reasoning for each system.
2. **Draft risk register entries** for visual inspection and the chatbot, structured to sit alongside the existing ISMS and QMS registers.
3. **At least two governed workflows:** inspection defect review with human sign-off, and chatbot escalation.
4. **A draft AI use procedure** and an evidence map that defines what each artifact must record for audit purposes.

These artifacts give Internal Audit concrete material to assess against the June 2026 finding. Whether the finding is closed remains Internal Audit's determination.

The work can also feed later ISO/IEC 42001 preparation. This program does not promise any certification or audit outcome, and final EU AI Act classification rests with Tamarack's counsel.

| Item | Detail |

| Format | Two days, live virtual, four 90-minute working sessions per day |
| Participants | The seven roles named above |
| Pre-work | Repository pointers and a request list of materials to bring, issued after confirmation |
| Price | US$12,500 |
| Budget fit | Sits within the US$80,000 approved for this fiscal year |
| Dates | Unknown. We recommend Q1 2027 to leave time to finish the drafts before the Q2 2027 production target. |

We ask you to confirm by 15 December 2026, in line with your decision timeline. Once confirmed, we will agree delivery dates, confirm the participant list and issue the pre-work packet. We are glad to hold a 30-minute call with you and the Head of Quality to confirm that the visual inspection framing matches the pilot's current state.

Human-made, for Easy Work, Simply Done.
